iv: Mass of a stack of coffee filters
note: Film the fall and measure speed over the last part, or time a long drop.

iv: Canopy area of a paper parachute
Release height of a toy car on a ramp
dv: Distance it rolls along the floor

iv: Drop height of a ball
Temperature of a tennis or squash ball
note: Warm or cool balls in water; the temperature changes quickly once out, so be fast and consistent.

iv: Air pressure inside a ball
note: Needs a pump with a pressure gauge.

iv: Load hung on the end of a clamped ruler (cantilever)
Overhanging length of a clamped ruler
dv: Deflection of the end under a fixed load

iv: Overhanging length of a clamped ruler with a mass on the end
Span of a ruler supported at both ends
dv: Sag at the middle under a fixed load

iv: Drop height of a ball bearing
dv: Diameter of the crater in sand or flour

iv: Diameter of a funnel’s opening
dv: Time for sand or rice to drain out

iv: Size of the vent hole in the top of a parachute
dv: Time to fall a fixed height
note: Keep the canopy, strings and load the same; drop from the same height each time.

iv: Diameter of an inflated balloon (total mass kept the same)
note: Tape on small masses so every balloon weighs the same; film the last metre of the fall.

iv: Height of each nut tied along a string
dv: Time until it hits a metal tray
note: Drop the whole string at once and record the clicks; read the times off the sound trace.

iv: Total mass in an Atwood machine (same mass difference)
note: A light pulley helps; time a fixed drop distance.

iv: Hanging mass pulling a trolley
dv: Angle of the water surface in a small tank riding on it
note: Photograph or film the tilted surface while the trolley speeds up.

iv: Time a block is left resting on a surface
dv: Force (or slope angle) needed to start it sliding
note: The effect is small, so measure the starting angle carefully and repeat a lot.

iv: Temperature of a rubber eraser or block
dv: Friction force when dragged at steady speed
note: Warm or cool it in a sealed bag in water, dry it, and test straight away.

iv: Water content of sand (% by mass)
dv: Angle of repose of a poured pile
note: Pour through a funnel at a fixed height and measure the height and base width of the cone.

iv: Falling mass driving a string-wound gravity car
note: Wind the string around the axle; keep the drop height the same.

iv: Radius of the axle the string is wound on (gravity car)
note: Wrap tape around the axle to make it thicker; film the car to find its top speed.

iv: Depth a nail is hammered into wood
dv: Force needed to pull it out
note: Pull it straight out with a spring balance or force sensor; use softwood and small nails.

iv: Impact angle of a marble fired down a tube into flour
note: A thin layer of cocoa on top of the flour makes the crater edge easy to photograph.

iv: Thickness of a foam crash cushion
dv: Peak deceleration of a trolley hitting it
note: A phone strapped to the trolley can record acceleration; release from the same height each time.

iv: Diameter of a toy-car loop track
dv: Minimum release height for the car to complete the loop
note: Raise the start height in small steps until it just makes it.

iv: Pull-back distance of a small rubber-band launcher
note: Keep it desk-sized with a soft projectile (pom-pom, foam ball); safety glasses on, aimed away from people.

iv: Counterweight mass of a desk-top trebuchet
note: Desk-sized only, soft projectile; agree the design and testing area first.

iv: Volume of water in a bottle rocket (same pump pressure)
note: Outdoors with an adult, launch pad and pump with a gauge; everyone stands well back.

iv: Width of the base of a tall block
dv: Lowest push height at which it tips over instead of sliding
note: Beyond SL content (torque): read up first. Push slowly and horizontally with a pencil.

iv: Ratio of inner to outer radius of a spool
dv: Pulling angle at which it switches from rolling forward to backward
note: Beyond SL content (torque): read up first. Wind thread on cotton reels or taped-up spools.

iv: Bounce number of a dropped ball
note: Record the bounces with a sound app (phyphox has an acoustic stopwatch) and read off the gaps.

iv: Release angle of a pendulum
Separation of the two strings of a bifilar pendulum
Number of coils of a hanging slinky
Radius of a ball rolling inside a large curved bowl
Area of a card attached to an oscillating mass on a spring
dv: Amplitude after a set number of oscillations (damping)

iv: Height of the coupling string between two pendulums
dv: Time for the swinging to swap from one pendulum to the other
note: Hang two equal pendulums from a slack string; set one going and time the energy transfer.

iv: Mass added to a rolling platform holding two metronomes
dv: Time for the metronomes to synchronise
note: Start them out of step on a board resting on two cans; film to see when they lock together.

iv: Release angle of a pendulum
note: Needs a force sensor and data logger.

iv: Length of the wire in a torsion pendulum
note: Beyond SL content (rotation): read up first. A ln-ln graph finds the power.

iv: Gap between two aluminium plates either side of a swinging magnet
dv: Number of swings until the amplitude halves
note: Beyond SL content (induction): read up first. Film the swings against a scale.

iv: Number of coils hanging below the point you hold a slinky
note: Hold the slinky at different coils and let the rest hang; measure the stretched length.

iv: Tension in a stretched horizontal slinky
dv: Speed of a pulse along it
note: Change the stretch, measure the tension with a spring balance and film the pulse.

iv: Temperature difference between hot water and the room
Volume of water in a cup
Thickness of insulation (layers) around a container
Temperature of a viscous liquid (honey, oil, syrup)
dv: Time for a ball to fall a fixed distance through it
note: Use a tall column so fall times are several seconds.

iv: Speed of the air from a fan (distance from the fan)
dv: Rate of cooling of a can of hot water
note: Measure air speed with an anemometer app or move the fan further away.

iv: Number of fins (aluminium strips) attached to a can of hot water
note: Same water volume and starting temperature each time.

iv: Starting temperature of water
dv: Time to freeze in a freezer
note: At home; same container, volume and shelf position each time.

iv: Length of a metal rod with one end in hot water
dv: Temperature rise at the far end after a fixed time
note: Insulate the rod; tape a thermometer probe to the far end.

iv: Thickness of a slab of potato or jelly
dv: Time for its centre to reach a set temperature
note: Put a probe in the centre and heat on a hot plate or in hot water.

iv: Salt concentration of water
note: Use an electric heater with a joulemeter, or the method of mixtures.

iv: Volume of water in an electric kettle
note: At home; a plug-in power meter gives the energy used. Work out the energy gained by the water.

iv: Fraction of a lid painted black (or shade of grey)
dv: Temperature rise of air in a can under a lamp
note: Same lamp distance and time; the lamp gets hot.

iv: Number of holes in a closed painted can (model car)
dv: Temperature rise in sunlight or under a lamp
note: Seal a thermometer into the can with Blu-tack.

iv: Number of clear plastic layers over a model solar water heater
note: Run all tests at the same time of day, or under the same lamp.

iv: Depth in a column of soil heated from the top
dv: Time delay before the temperature peaks
note: Switch a heat lamp on and off and log temperatures at several depths.

iv: Temperature of a hot plate
dv: Lifetime of a water drop on it
note: Supervised only: hot plate above 200 °C. Drop water from a pipette and film the drops.

iv: Volume of water in a wine glass
Length of the air column in a tube partly filled with water
Distance from a speaker
note: Work outdoors or in a large room; reflections spoil it.

iv: Air temperature in a long pipe
note: Clap or click at the open end of a pipe closed at the far end; read the echo delay from a recording.

iv: Diameter of a pipe
note: Find two resonant lengths for the same frequency in each pipe; tone-generator app as the source.

iv: Length of a metal rod struck on its end
note: Hold the rod at its middle; a spectrum app picks out the main frequency.

iv: Length of a xylophone-style bar (wood or metal)
note: Support the bar on foam at about a quarter of its length from each end.

iv: Tension in a stretched string
note: Hang masses over a pulley to set the tension; use a frequency app.

iv: Volume of air in a bottle
dv: Frequency when you blow across the top
note: Add water to change the air volume; measure the volume left each time.

iv: Number of towels or cushions in a small room or box
note: Pop a balloon or clap and record how long the sound takes to die away.

iv: Thickness of a foam or fabric layer
dv: Drop in sound level through it
note: Tone app on one phone inside a box, sound meter app outside. Two phones needed.

iv: Frequency of a tone
dv: Sound level getting through a fixed barrier
note: Same set-up as the thickness idea; keep the speaker volume fixed.

iv: Frequency of a tone from two speakers
note: Work outdoors or in a large room; walk a sound meter along a line in front of the speakers.

iv: Length of a string telephone
dv: Sound level at the far cup
note: Keep the string tight and the source tone fixed.

iv: Amplitude of a pendulum carrying a buzzer
dv: Largest change in frequency heard (Doppler shift)
note: Record with a spectrogram app placed in line with the swing.

iv: Rotation rate of a buzzer on a spinning arm
note: The arm must be guarded and the buzzer fixed firmly.

iv: Distance from a small bulb
note: Use a phone light-sensor app in a dark room.

iv: Angle between two polarising filters
Number of sheets of plastic or glass
Distance from a hair (or slit) to the screen
dv: Width of the central bright band
note: Laser pointer: never point it at eyes. Ask before using one.

iv: Temperature of a small solar cell
Colour (wavelength) of an LED
dv: Voltage at which it starts to glow

iv: Angle between two mirrors
note: Hinge two small mirrors with tape and stand an object between them.

iv: Real depth of water in a tall container
dv: Apparent depth of a coin at the bottom
note: Find the apparent depth by lining up a pin seen beside the container (no parallax).

iv: Sugar (or salt) concentration of a solution
note: Use a ray box and a clear rectangular container; measure angles of incidence and refraction.

iv: Depth (path length) of a sugar syrup between polarising filters
dv: Angle the light’s polarisation is rotated
note: Rotate the second filter to the darkest position and read the angle.

iv: Bend radius of a plastic optical fibre or acrylic rod
dv: Light intensity coming out the end
note: Bend it around jars of different sizes; phone light sensor in a dark room.

iv: Angle of a small solar cell to a lamp
note: Measure V and I across a fixed resistor; keep the lamp distance fixed.

iv: Mass of dust spread on a small solar cell
note: Sieve fine powder (flour, sand) evenly over a clear sheet laid on the cell.

iv: Object distance from a magnifying lens
note: Use a lit object and a screen; measure image and object heights.

iv: Distance from a magnet
note: A phone magnetometer app measures B. Subtract the background (Earth’s) field.

iv: Current in a coil
Temperature of a magnet
Wall thickness (or material) of a copper or aluminium pipe
dv: Time for a strong magnet to fall through it
note: Fall times of several seconds make hand timing workable.

iv: Resistance in an RC circuit
dv: Time for the capacitor’s voltage to halve
note: Large capacitors make times long enough to read a multimeter.

iv: Temperature of a battery
Height a magnet falls through a coil
note: Needs a data logger fast enough to catch the peak.

iv: Distance between two magnets
note: Put one magnet on a digital scale and lower the other on a stand above it.

iv: Number of turns per metre of a stretched slinky carrying a current
note: Low-voltage supply only; measure the field with a phone magnetometer app and subtract the background.

iv: Current in two long parallel wires
note: Needs large currents from a low-voltage supply and a sensitive balance; only with Mr. Holmes.

iv: Length of a pencil line drawn on paper
note: Shade a thick, even line with a soft pencil and use a multimeter.

iv: Number of layers of pencil shading
note: Same strip size and pencil each time; multimeter on the resistance range.

iv: Temperature of a coil of thin copper wire
note: Seal the coil in a bag or test tube in a water bath; use enough wire for a resistance of several ohms.

iv: Temperature difference between the two junctions of a thermocouple
note: Twist copper and iron wires together; ice water and a water bath set the junction temperatures.

iv: Capacitance (or resistance) in a 555 timer circuit
note: A cheap kit works; time many flashes and divide.

iv: Voltage across a small DC motor
note: Count rotations with a slow-motion video of a marked shaft or a phone strobe app.

iv: Number of magnets stacked in a homopolar motor
note: The battery and wire get hot quickly, so run each test for a few seconds only.

iv: Layers of aluminium foil under a slope
dv: Time for a strong magnet to slide down it
note: Beyond SL content (induction): read up first. Compare with a plastic slope as a control.

iv: Gap between a magnet on a toy car and an aluminium ramp
dv: Time to roll down the ramp
note: Beyond SL content (induction): read up first. Change the gap with spacers under the magnet.

iv: Number of turns on a coil
dv: Peak voltage induced by a magnet spinning next to it
note: Beyond SL content (induction): read up first. Needs a data logger or oscilloscope.

iv: Number of turns on the secondary coil of a low-voltage transformer
note: Beyond SL content: read up first. Lab low-voltage AC supply only, never mains.

iv: Number of iron rods pushed into a coil on low-voltage AC
note: Beyond SL content (self-inductance): read up first. Lab low-voltage AC supply only.

iv: Distance between a model guitar pickup and a vibrating steel string
note: Beyond SL content (induction): read up first. Needs an oscilloscope or data logger.

iv: Time since a bottle started draining through a small hole
Inner diameter of a siphon tube
Drop height of a water droplet
dv: Rebound height from a water surface

iv: Height of water above a hole in a bottle
note: Keep the height of the hole above the landing surface the same.

iv: Diameter of a hole in a bottle
dv: Time to drain a fixed volume
note: Drill or punch clean holes; time from the same starting level.

iv: Length of a narrow tube draining a container
note: Keep the water level in the container constant (top it up) and collect water for a fixed time.

iv: Height difference between the two ends of a siphon
note: Same tube throughout; measure the volume collected in a fixed time.

iv: Diameter of the hole in a floating cup
dv: Time for the cup to fill and sink
note: Plastic plumbing caps drilled with different holes work well.

iv: Diameter of a ball bearing
dv: Terminal velocity falling through syrup or glycerol
note: Use a tall column and time the fall between two marks low down.

iv: Water added to honey or syrup (% by mass)
dv: Time for a ball to fall a fixed distance
note: Mix well and let bubbles rise out before timing.

iv: Detergent concentration
dv: Mass of a water drop falling from a tube
note: Weigh 20 drops at once to get the mass of one; same tube throughout.

iv: Temperature of water
dv: Mass of a drop falling from a tube
note: Weigh 20 drops at once; work quickly so the temperature stays steady.

iv: Angle of attack of a card wing in front of a fan
note: Mount the wing on a digital scale and read the drop in reading.

iv: Hanging mass towing a model boat across water
note: Use a pulley at the edge of a long tub or bath; time a marked length.

iv: Angle of a sail on a trolley in front of a fan
note: Hold the trolley with a spring balance and read the force.

iv: Number of blades on a model wind turbine
dv: Output voltage across a fixed resistor
note: A small motor works as the generator; keep the fan distance fixed.

iv: Blade angle (pitch) of a model wind turbine
note: Measure V across a fixed resistor and work out V²/R.

iv: Height water falls onto a model water wheel
dv: Time to lift a small mass a fixed height
note: Keep the flow rate steady; work out the output power from the lift.

iv: Number of steel balls behind the magnet in a magnetic “gun”
dv: Speed of the ball launched off the end
note: Strong magnets pinch and the ball flies: safety glasses, aim at a soft stop. Film the launch.

iv: Mass on a rubber-band bungee cord
note: Film against a ruler; drop from the same point each time.

iv: Volume of water heated in a microwave (fixed time)
note: At home; stir before reading. Compare with the oven’s rated power.

iv: Number of craft sticks glued into a laminated beam
dv: Sag at the middle under a fixed load
note: Test the beam flat and on its edge as a second variable.

iv: Span between supports of a spaghetti strand
note: Hang a cup at the middle and add rice or small masses slowly.

iv: Number of spaghetti strands in a bundle
note: Tape the ends of the bundle; same span each time.

iv: Diameter of a rolled paper tube (same sheet of paper)
note: Load the top slowly with masses on a board.

iv: Diameter of fishing line
note: Same brand and length; protect feet and eyes, and stack masses low.

iv: Temperature of a rubber band
note: Hang it in a tall beaker of water at different temperatures.

iv: Maximum load on a rubber band
dv: Energy lost in one stretch-and-relax cycle
note: Record extension while loading and unloading; the energy lost is the area between the two curves.
